questions.key_step: Bernoulli reduction then integration by parts; routine but long (several linked stages).
questions.justification: Bernoulli reduction $t=y^{-2}$, integrating factor $x^2$, integration by parts, constant and algebraic matching of the option: four linked stages (L3 relative to the Main-level bank).

questions.key_step: Locate where $\sin x\ge|\cos x-\sin x|$, split at $\frac\pi4$, evaluate at $\tan x=\frac12$.
questions.justification: Two-piece area with modulus; the lower limit $\tan^{-1}\frac12$ is not obvious and the surd arithmetic needs care (L2).

questions.key_step: Integrating factor $e^{\alpha t}$; both terms of the solution decay.
questions.justification: Standard first-order linear equation, then a limit of decaying exponentials (L1).

questions.key_step: Split $|x-t|$ at $t=x$ for three ranges of $x$; the minimum is at the interior critical point $x=1$.
questions.justification: Three-case integral of a modulus exponent followed by minimisation; a few linked steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Two linear conditions in $b$, $c$: the integral and $P(2)=5$.
questions.justification: Two linear equations from an integral and the remainder theorem (L1).

questions.key_step: Factor $\sin^n\theta$ out of the root so that $d\left(1-\sin^{1-n}\theta\right)$ appears.
questions.justification: Algebraic rearrangement then a power substitution with symbolic $n$ (L2).

questions.key_step: $t=y^2$ gives $(xt)'=\frac1x$.
questions.justification: One substitution to a linear equation with a simple integrating factor, then matching the form of the answer (L2).

questions.key_step: Separable: $\frac{1+y^2}{y^2}dy=\frac{e^x}{e^x+1}dx$.
questions.justification: Direct separation of variables and two standard integrals (L1).

questions.key_step: Identify the pieces on $\left[\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right]$: line $1-x$ above parabola; area $=$ trapezium $-$ parabola area.
questions.justification: Piecewise function plus a parabola, surds in the limits; two area pieces (L2).

questions.key_step: Divide by $x^2$: the numerator $2x-x^{-2}$ is the derivative of $x^2+x^{-1}$.
questions.justification: Single recognised substitution, no further work (L2 relative to the bank: the division by $x^2$ must be seen).

questions.key_step: Horizontal strips: width $\sqrt y-\frac y2$; equate the integrals below and above $y=\alpha$.
questions.justification: Area bisection with strip integration and a fractional-power equation (L2).

questions.key_step: Reduce to a linear equation with IF $x^{-1/2}$, then substitute $x=u^4$ and $u^3=t$.
questions.justification: Linear equation with fractional powers, two nested substitutions and a constant-fitting stage (L3).

questions.key_step: King-type pairing $x\to\pi-x$ halves the integral because the bracket is symmetric about $\frac\pi2$.
questions.justification: Recognising the $1/(1+5^{\cos x})$ symmetry and then trigonometric product-to-sum reduction; two ideas combined (L3).

questions.key_step: By parts: $20I_n+nI_{n-1}=e^{20}$; subtract two consecutive cases.
questions.justification: Standard reduction formula by parts and elimination of the constant (L2).

questions.key_step: Split at $x=0$, where $x(3-x)$ changes sign; take absolute values.
questions.justification: Single-parabola area with one sign change (L1).

questions.key_step: With $t=e^{\sin y}$ the equation is $t'+t\cos x=\cos x$, whose solution through the initial data is $t\equiv1$.
questions.justification: One substitution; the initial condition collapses the solution to $y\equiv0$ (L2: the substitution is hidden).

questions.key_step: $1-\cos2x=2\sin^2x$ and $t=\cos x$ give $-\sqrt2\int\frac{dt}{\sqrt{2t^2-1}}$; then match the form by squaring.
questions.justification: Trigonometric rewriting, a standard $\sqrt{2t^2-1}$ integral, and a non-trivial rearrangement to match the given form (L3).

questions.key_step: Tangent intercept $c=f-bf'$; $bc=3$ gives $\left(\frac fb\right)'=-\frac3{b^3}$, an exact derivative.
questions.justification: Translate a tangent condition to an ODE, spot the exact derivative, then use two points on the curve (L3).

questions.key_step: Symmetry about $x=\frac12$; limits $\frac13$ to $\frac12$ with lower curve $(1-x)^2$.
questions.justification: Three-curve region with symmetry; limits need care but the integral is polynomial (L2).

questions.key_step: $x=\frac1{1+t}$ converts the Beta integral to $\int_0^\infty$; fold $[1,\infty)$ back with $t\to\frac1t$.
questions.justification: Beta-function substitution and fold-back symmetry; the idea is not routine for Main-level students (L3).
